holidays.name: National Fritters Day
holidays.description: Today is for deep-fried batter wrapped around good things. Apple, corn, banana, clam and cashew fritters all count. Fry up a batch, dust them with powdered sugar or dunk them in syrup, and eat them while they're still hot and crackly.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance, and nobody has pinned down who started it. It exists to honor the fritter, which cooks around the world have made in many forms for centuries.
holidays.funFact: Fritters turn up in almost every cuisine. Examples include Indian pakoras, Caribbean conch fritters, Southern corn fritters and Dutch appelbeignets. Almost anything can become a fritter once it's battered and fried.

holidays.name: National Mutt Day
holidays.description: This day celebrates mixed-breed dogs, the lovable one-of-a-kind pups with mystery ancestry and wildly mismatched features. It also encourages people to adopt a mutt from a shelter or rescue instead of buying a dog.
holidays.origin: Pet and lifestyle expert Colleen Paige founded National Mutt Day to draw attention to the millions of mixed-breed dogs in shelters that need homes. It is observed twice a year, on July 31 and December 2.
holidays.funFact: No two mutts are exactly alike. A mixed-breed dog can be a surprising blend of floppy ears, curly tails and odd markings that no purebred standard would ever allow.
